audit_findings.title: Equity-affiliate earnings may be double counted through the $10.936 billion stakes add-on
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.936 billion stakes add-on at risk; exact duplicated amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate earnings or distributions enter owner earnings while the bridge separately adds the value of the same affiliates.
audit_findings.evidence: The Chemicals segment consists of our 50% interest in CPChem, which we account for under the equity method.
audit_findings.explanation: Double counting is not yet demonstrated because the owner-earnings reconciliation is absent. It is reasonably capable of materially overstating value: the stakes add-on equals $27.04 per share and 52.7% of the $20.742 billion base equity value. CPChem alone had a $7.899 billion carrying value at year-end 2025, while PSX reported $762 million of total affiliate earnings and $971 million of affiliate distributions during 2025.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each affiliate's earnings, distributions and capital spending through owner earnings. Rerun using one mutually exclusive treatment: exclude affiliate cash flows and add independently valued stakes, or retain affiliate cash flows and omit the corresponding stakes. Reconcile each stake value to affiliate debt and noncontrolling claims.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor combines materially different pre- and post-transaction perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.5 billion of acquisitions and $3.5 billion of disposition proceeds in 2025; pro forma owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Partial-year acquired and disposed operations distort recurring earnings, maintenance capital and the owner-earnings anchor subsequently grown in every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: We funded capital expenditures and investments of $2.2 billion, completed acquisitions of $3.5 billion, net of cash acquired and received proceeds from asset dispositions of $3.5 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed perimeter is demonstrated: Coastal Bend was acquired April 1, WRB became fully consolidated October 1, and 65% of Germany and Austria Marketing was sold December 1, while perimeter is recorded as null. The direction cannot be established because annualizing acquired operations raises both earnings and capital requirements, while removing disposed operations can raise or lower owner earnings. With only a $406.2 million anchor, the unresolved pro forma adjustment is reasonably capable of materially changing the operating valuation.
audit_findings.action: Build a twelve-month post-closing owner-earnings base using quarterly segment results and cash-flow detail, annualizing Coastal Bend and full WRB, removing disposed operations and transaction gains, and matching maintenance capital and working capital to that same perimeter; then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains only a partial-year cost for $2 billion of new junior subordinated capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $120.75 million annual pretax coupon; approximately $86 million pretax annualization shortfall in 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated recurring interest deduction inflates equity-level owner earnings and every forecast year derived from the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: On September 18, 2025, Phillips 66 Company, a wholly owned subsidiary of Phillips 66, issued $2 billion aggregate principal amount of junior subordinated notes that are fully and unconditionally guaranteed by Phillips 66.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: the notes were issued September 18, 2025, so the latest-actual anchor contains only about three and a half months of their recurring coupon. The annual coupon is 29.7% of the $406.2 million anchor, and the approximately $86 million pretax shortfall is 21.2% of that anchor before tax and capitalized-interest effects. The June 2026 filing still reports the notes outstanding, although the exact normalized after-tax cost is unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Replace recorded 2025 interest for both series with a full-year run-rate charge, determine the deductible and capitalized portions, apply the appropriate tax effect, incorporate contractual reset floors, and rerun all scenarios using the normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement and environmental cash claims may be absent from both owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.227 billion booked at 2025-12-31; exact valuation omission unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Settlement cash may be omitted after depreciation is added back, or the remaining obligation may need a single bridge deduction ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Most of our asset retirement obligations are not expected to be paid until many years in the future and are expected to be funded from general company resources at the time of removal.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes $721 million of AROs and $506 million of environmental accruals, equal to $3.03 per share and 5.9% of base equity value, but it does not establish that these amounts were omitted. PSX also recorded $84 million of ARO spending and $937 million of environmental expense in 2025, which may already flow through owner earnings. Payment timing, tax effects and overlap with earnings, capital expenditure and the bridge remain unresolved, so the record cannot establish the net valuation impact.
audit_findings.action: Trace ARO and remediation accretion, depreciation, expense, capital expenditure and settlement cash through the owner-earnings workpapers. Deduct only uncovered future cash claims once, either through normalized owner earnings or the bridge, and rerun if the resulting adjustment is material.

audit_findings.title: Propel Fuels requires mutually exclusive normalization and liability treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: $262 million 2025 charge; $928 million accrued liability at 2026-06-30
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining a one-time charge in the recurring anchor understates owner earnings, while adding it back without deducting or scheduling the legal claim overstates the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the August 2025 final judgment and the October 2024 jury verdict, we recorded $262 million and $604.9 million of expense for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, which are included within the “Selling, general and administrative expenses” line on our consolidated statement of income and reported in the M&S segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge and obligation are demonstrated, but their valuation treatment is not. The $262 million charge equals 64.5% of the $406.2 million anchor, so perpetuating it can materially understate operating value. Conversely, the latest accrued claim is $928 million, or $2.29 per share, and increased $61 million during the first half of 2026 as post-judgment interest and other amounts accumulated. Omitting that claim after normalizing earnings would overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $262 million charge remains in the anchor. If it does, add back its nonrecurring after-tax effect and deduct the $928 million accrued claim once, updated for post-judgment interest and awarded fees, or model the same obligation as dated cash outflows. Rerun without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow adjustments may not match the common-equity earnings claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $125 million of 2025 NCI income and $164 million of 2025 NCI distributions; net owner-earnings error unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Owner earnings can mix net income attributable to Phillips 66 with 100% consolidated depreciation, capital expenditure and working-capital movements belonging partly to noncontrolling owners.
audit_findings.evidence: A significant portion of our business is conducted through DCP LP, a consolidated subsidiary in which we hold an aggregate direct and indirect economic interest of 86.8%.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates different ownership bases: DCP LP is consolidated although PSX owns an 86.8% economic interest, and 2025 net income attributable to noncontrolling interests was $125 million, equal to 30.8% of the $406.2 million anchor. Whether the owner-earnings adjustments were ownership-scaled is unresolved. Because consolidated depreciation was $3.251 billion and capital expenditures were $2.233 billion, even a modest mismatch within those adjustments is reasonably capable of materially changing the small anchor; the direction depends on the relative NCI shares of depreciation, capital spending and working capital.
audit_findings.action: Recompute every historical owner-earnings component on one consistent basis: either start with consolidated net income and deduct noncontrolling owners' shares of all cash flows, or start with income attributable to Phillips 66 and ownership-scale every add-back and deduction by entity. Recalculate the anchor and rerun all scenarios.
